content.title: AKU-EB hosts summer camp
content.subtitle: Public-private partnerships essential to wipe out illiteracy

content.text: "The 21st century is the century of partnerships and the public and private sectors should join hands to reduce illiteracy," said Ghulam Farid Khatiya, Minister of State for Education. He mentioned that the public sector alone was not responsible for improving the literacy rate in Pakistan which at 48 per cent was one of the lowest of developing countries in the region. Instead it is a joint responsibility of all stakeholders including the private sector. The Minister made these remarks at the inaugural ceremony of the 10th National Summer Camp for Talented HSSC Boys, with 150 students from 26 education boards across Pakistan, hosted by the Aga Khan University Examination Board (AKU-EB).

Explaining the government's plans to reform the education sector, Khatiya talked about the Ministry's efforts to make the education system more demand and market oriented, to meet the needs of the time. He informed the group that the existing Scheme of Studies for classes I to XII has been revised according to emerging trends, global changes and job market requirements. The new Scheme will give importance to the sciences along with Islamic studies. It will also include issues related to cultural sensitivity, health, environment and population education, and peace and human rights. The Minister encouraged students to continue to achieve excellent results and "to earn a good name for the nation."

The theme of this year's summer camp will be an introduction to universities and what students should be thinking about as they approach a university education. Dr Thomas Christie, Director, AKU-EB highlighted that students "need to have a problem-oriented approach to life" to be ready with creative, innovative solutions to real life needs. He pointed out the important role of education in helping students address current market demands and preparing them for higher education and employment. The five-day camp includes sessions meant to introduce students to "professionals that have the same education and background as you have but are doing interesting things and earning a living from it" such as professional bloggers. Other events encourage students to use their creative abilities in music and art or even to translate scientific ideas into easy-to-understand messages e.g. too little electricity and so much sun, how can solar energy be put to use in Pakistan.

Every year, the IBCC (Inter-Board Committee of Chairmen) requests one of its 30 members - all the Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education in Pakistan - to host a summer camp for the top six students of each Board, based on their SSC examination results from the previous year.  This year AKU-EB was the host.
